one-check-per-line.why: all 7 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 7

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 7 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I compared each of the seven checks' PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests only exit=0 and a byte-exact cmp of `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n`, which is what line 1 says. Checks 2–5 test only byte-exact output and don't add an exit-code test the lines don't state. Check 5's `printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n'` correctly produces the JSON tab escape. Check 6 requires `npm test` to exit 0 plus a test that runs the CLI with --tsv on tab input and "asserts on its stdout", which matches "checks its output". Check 7 requires only that the flag is described and an example uses it. "such as `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`" is only an illustration. The stricter items (other arguments alongside the flag, README saying "tab-separated", no quoting/--sep/--help) all sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)". None of the checks adds a stricter requirement.

runs-as-written.why: The criterion holds for both briefs. I checked every command in them against the repository. Every file they name exists at this commit: bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js, README.md and package.json. `npm test` maps to the "test": "node --test" script. In check 5, `printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n'` inside single quotes prints a literal backslash-t, which is the JSON tab escape the output should contain. The verifier says to use bash, so the `cmp - <(...)` process substitution is valid. `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` and the same grep on README.md are valid. The builder's JavaScript (`process.argv.slice(2)`, `parse(text, '\t')`, and the escaped test strings) is valid. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is an example for the README, not a command to run. The advisory `node bin/csv2json.js x --tsv` has no input piped in, so run alone it would wait on stdin. It is only an example idea outside PASS/FAIL, so I don't count it as a broken command.

catches-traps.why: Both must_catch items are handled. Item 1: the builder brief names test/csv.test.js, says "Keep the existing tests" and has the builder run `npm test` to exit 0. It also ties src/parse.js to the CSV path: "Leave src/parse.js alone unless you really have to change it, and if you do, the CSV behaviour must stay the same." That covers keeping the CSV path safe through the shared parse(). The brief never says outright that parse() is shared, but its wording keeps CSV behaviour fixed if parse.js changes, and the existing tests must still pass. Item 2: verifier Check 6 runs "npm test; echo "exit=$?"", not proof 6's undefined `npm run test:cli`, then greps test/*.js for --tsv.

avoids-must-not.why: Both must_not items are avoided. Item 1: no verifier check depends on `npm run test:cli`. Check 6 runs `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and greps test/*.js, so it follows the expect line rather than the proof's test:cli command. `test:cli` does not appear anywhere in either brief. Item 2: the builder brief never asks for a general separator option. Step 2 says "do not add auto-detection, --sep/--delimiter or --help". Step 1 only checks for '--tsv' and calls parse(text, '\t'). The verifier's advisory also says the diff "should not add quoting rules, --sep". Neither brief breaks either item.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's PASS/FAIL conditions and probes. The builder brief has no cmp/process-substitution commands. It has no "PASS:"/"FAIL:" wording and none of the verifier's grep commands (`grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js`, `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md`). The input/output pairs the builder must cover in its own tests come straight from the issue's expect lines. Writing its own tests and running the expect-line commands are both allowed. The README example `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` and "reads tab-separated input" come from the wording of issue proof 7, so they set the bar rather than leak a check. "Anywhere in process.argv" comes from assumption 2, not from the verifier's advisory probe (`x --tsv`). Telling the builder to run `npm test` and the acceptance commands is allowed. Nothing exclusive to the verifier leaks.
